title: Passive electrical transfer gave no clear response detection prediction gain in 15384 selected worm pairs
abstract: We tested whether a passive electrical transfer score adds prediction value for detected evoked responses after direct counts and cell identity are known. We linked the wild-type Randi atlas to two adult Witvliet maps by cell name. The sample had 15384 ordered pairs and 837 detections. Five validation folds kept both directions of each pair together. Base mean log loss was 0.181290. The added score reduced loss by 0.000044, with a conditional 95 percent node bootstrap interval of -0.001046 to 0.001230. Seven sensitivity checks also gave intervals across zero. These results do not establish added prediction value for the tested score. Different animals supplied anatomy and activity. Incomplete electrical annotation, assumed conductance and leak, model choice, and uncertainty that holds predictions fixed limit the test. New code, aggregate results, a figure and exact external retrieval instructions support reproduction. Source records and derived pair tables remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Added passive electrical transfer gave no clear log-loss gain. Bars are conditional 95 percent node bootstrap intervals, with fitted predictions held fixed.
